title: Cybersecurity & Web Defense Quiz
description: Validate your ability to identify and eliminate web vulnerabilities, authentication flaws, and API exploits.

questions.question: What makes Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) the most dangerous API vulnerability according to OWASP?
options: It forces the client browser to download unauthorized cryptocurrency miners.
The API authenticates the user, but fails to check whether the authenticated user actually has permission to read or modify the specific requested resource ID.
It overflows the CPU registers on the server, causing a physical hardware crash.
It disables HTTPS encryption for all users on the domain.
questions.explanation: With BOLA/IDOR, an attacker is legitimately logged in, but by simply changing `/api/documents/100` to `/api/documents/101`, they gain access to another customer's private data because the backend failed to verify resource ownership against the session subject.

questions.question: Why should passwords NEVER be hashed using fast cryptographic hash functions like SHA-256 or MD5 in production?
options: Because SHA-256 and MD5 produce non-alphanumeric characters that crash SQL databases.
Because modern GPUs and ASIC rigs can calculate billions of SHA-256 hashes per second, allowing attackers to crack password databases via brute-force and rainbow tables.
Because SHA-256 is deprecated by the W3C consortium.
Because SHA-256 passwords can be decrypted using an SSL private key.
questions.explanation: Fast hash functions are engineered for high-throughput checksum verification. Passwords require computationally expensive, memory-hard algorithms like Argon2id or Bcrypt with deliberate work factors (costs) and salts, which dramatically slows down offline GPU cracking attacks.
